testCase.question: Per NYC BC 1019.3, Exception 2, are we permitted to have the open stair as shown, provided that the required draft curtain is installed?
testCase.expectedConclusion: Potentially, but not on the basis stated. BC 1019.3 establishes a general enclosure rule. Exception 2 is a distinct potential pathway for an unenclosed exit access stair between only the first and second stories above grade in a building sprinklered throughout under Section 903.3.1.1, subject to its independent-exit, separation-from-other-stories, and remoteness conditions. Exception 2 does not contain a draft-curtain requirement. The draft curtain and closely spaced sprinklers appear in Exception 4, which is a different compliance pathway with different conditions. Permitext cannot confirm the project's compliance until the occupancy and the material facts for the selected pathway are established.

answer.answerText:
Not on the stated basis. The draft-curtain provision is Exception 4—not Exception 2—to BC 1019.3. Exception 2 permits an unenclosed exit-access stair only where the building is sprinklered throughout under BC 903.3.1.1; the stair serves only between the first and second stories above grade; both stories have the required number of approved independent exits under BC 1006, and never fewer than two means of egress; the interconnected stories are not open to other stories; and the unenclosed stair is remotely located under BC 1007. A draft curtain does not substitute for any of those Exception 2 conditions.

If the proposal instead relies on Exception 4, an open exit-access stair may be permitted only if the building is sprinklered throughout in accordance with BC 903.3.1.1; the vertical-opening area is no more than twice the stair’s horizontal projected area; and the opening has both a draft curtain and closely spaced sprinklers complying with NFPA 13 as modified by Appendix Q. In occupancies other than Groups B and M, the opening cannot connect more than four stories. The general rule remains that exit-access stairs in the scope of BC 1019.3 must be shaft-enclosed.

The supplied material does not include the drawing or identify the occupancy, sprinkler-system compliance, stories connected, opening-area comparison, or—as applicable—the independent-exit, story-openness, and remoteness conditions. Therefore, it cannot establish that the stair as shown qualifies under either exception.
answer.conclusion: Not on the stated basis. The draft-curtain provision is Exception 4—not Exception 2—to BC 1019.3. Exception 2 permits an unenclosed exit-access stair only where the building is sprinklered throughout under BC 903.3.1.1; the stair serves only between the first and second stories above grade; both stories have the required number of approved independent exits under BC 1006, and never fewer than two means of egress; the interconnected stories are not open to other stories; and the unenclosed stair is remotely located under BC 1007. A draft curtain does not substitute for any of those Exception 2 conditions.

supportedPoints.heading: Baseline enclosure requirement
supportedPoints.explanation: For occupancies other than Groups H, I-2 and I-3, exit access stairways and ramps must be enclosed with a shaft enclosure complying with Section 713, unless an applicable exception permits otherwise.

supportedPoints.heading: Exception 2 does not use a draft-curtain alternative
supportedPoints.explanation: Exception 2 permits exit access stairways and ramps only in a building equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1, where they serve only between the first and second stories above grade; both stories have the required approved independent exits under Section 1006 and at least two means of egress; the interconnected stories are not open to other stories; and the unenclosed stairways or ramps are remotely located under Section 1007.

supportedPoints.heading: Draft curtain is an Exception 4 condition
supportedPoints.explanation: Exception 4 permits exit access stairways and ramps in a building equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 where the vertical-opening area does not exceed twice the horizontal projected area of the stairway or ramp, and the opening is protected by both a draft curtain and closely spaced sprinklers in accordance with NFPA 13 as modified by Appendix Q. In occupancies other than Groups B and M, the opening may not connect more than four stories.

AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression or control device that operates automatically when its heat-activated element is heated to its thermal rating or above, allowing water to discharge over a specified area. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. EXIT ACCESS STAIRWAY. A stairway within the exit access portion of the means of egress system. MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from any occupied portion of a building or structure to a public way. A means of egress consists of three separate and distinct parts: the exit access, the exit and the exit discharge. OPEN PARKING GARAGE . A structure or portion of a structure with the openings as described in Section 406 . 5 . 2 that is used for the parking or storage of private motor vehicles as described in Section 406 . 5.3 . PARKING GARAGE. A structure or portion of a structure, other than a private garage or carport, used for the parking or storage of motor vehicles. SHAFT ENCLOSURE. The walls or construction forming the boundaries of a shaft.

1009.3 1009.3 Exit stairways. To be considered part of an accessible means of egress, a stairway between stories shall have a clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum between handrails and shall either incorporate an area of rescue assistance within an enlarged floor-level landing or shall be accessed from an area of rescue assistance complying with Section 1009.6. Exit access stairways that connect levels in the same story are not permitted as part of an accessible means of egress. Exceptions: The following exceptions apply to the requirements of clear width and area of rescue assistance, and do not supersede the other requirements of the accessible means of egress: 1. Exit access stairways providing means of egress from mezzanines are permitted as part of an accessible means of egress. 2. The clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) between handrails and the area of rescue assistance is not required at exit access stairways as permitted by Section 1017 or exit stairways in buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. 3. The clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) between handrails is not required for interior exit stairways accessed from a refuge area in conjunction with a horizontal exit. 4. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at exit access stairways where two-way communication is provided at the elevator landing in accordance with Section 1009.8. 5. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at stairways in buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. 6. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at stairways serving open parking garages. 7. Areas of rescue assistance are not required for smoke-protected assembly seating areas complying with Section 1029.6.2. 8. Areas of rescue assistance are not required in Group R-2 occupancies. 9. Where the provisions of this code require that a building or portion thereof be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with this section, sprinklers shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13 except as provided in Sections 903.3.1.1.1 and 903.2 of this code. Where allowed in buildings of Group R, up to and including six stories in height, automatic sprinkler systems shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13R. The number of stories of Group R occupancies constructed in accordance with Sections 510.2 and 510.4 shall be measured from the horizontal assembly creating separate buildings.

903.3.1.3 903.3.1.3 NFPA 13D sprinkler systems. Where allowed, automatic sprinkler systems in one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses, up to and including six stories in height, shall be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13D.
